_readme: Licences for scripts/singleton_slot_preflight.py (playhead-mfeq, SHAPE 2).
A `why` must say WHAT BOUNDS THE POPULATION TO ONE. 'It is fine' is not a
reason; 'the slot IS the reentry guard, and here is the line that enforces
it' is. Two of the seven entries below are not licences at all — they name
a filed bead, so the amnesty is visibly temporary rather than quietly
permanent.
THE LIST IS CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A new match fails the gate, and an
entry that matches nothing ALSO fails it: a licence for a field nobody can
find was renamed or moved, and whatever inherits the name inherits the
amnesty. Same rule gate_baseline.py applies to a baseline member that did
not run.
MEASURED BEFORE THE RULE WAS WRITTEN, per this repo's own admission rule.
On b5e04fc6, over Playhead/: 56 matches of ^(current|pending|last)[A-Z] on
an optional stored var across all type kinds, of which 11 were on actors.
Correcting the scanner to exclude function-LOCAL vars (3 false positives:
ShadowRetryObserver.lastSeen, AnalysisAudioService.lastInputBlockError, and
one struct) took the totals to 47 and 8. playhead-mfeq removed three of the
eight (AnalysisWorkScheduler.currentJobId / currentEpisodeId /
pendingCancelCause) and added one DEBUG-only observation slot, leaving the
6 pre-existing entries here plus that one. The un-allowlisted count is 0,
so the rule ships ENABLED rather than as a red tier.
The 40 non-actor matches are NOT enforced and are NOT listed here — see the
module docstring for why, and `--report-all` for the standing count.

allow.why: NOT A LICENCE — a live instance, filed as playhead-2kxd (P1). The file says so itself in three places: 'that actor state may belong to the previous episode' (~11292), 'an interleaving updatePriors / recordSuccessfulObservation turn could rewrite currentPodcastProfile between the two reads' (~12876), and a public setter deleted in review because it 'could clobber an in-flight updatePriors' (~2050). Three rounds have each hardened one READ SITE and left the slot. Out of playhead-mfeq's scope, which was the three AnalysisWorkScheduler fields; allowlisted so the rule can ship green while 2kxd carries the fix.

Compiled only under #if DEBUG, and read by nothing but its own test accessor — so a production path that reaches for it FAILS TO COMPILE in Release, which is the guarantee rather than a convention. It records the last broadcast cancelCurrentJob(cause:), which is a fact about the CALL and has no per-job answer when the broadcast reached no jobs at all (BackgroundGrantBudgetTests asks exactly that of a BGTask expiry). The per-job cause it replaced lives on RunningJob.cancelCause. Listed rather than exempted by name because a rule that skips anything ending in ForTesting is a rule anyone can opt out of by renaming.

An eviction HEURISTIC, not an identity any answer is derived from. Every lookup keys on BandKey(episodeId:bandCenterTick:), which carries the episode id in full, so a stale value here cannot return another episode's features — the worst it can do with two episodes interleaved is thrash the cache and cost hit rate. Correctness is carried by the fully-qualified key; this slot only decides when to wipe.

THE SLOT IS WHAT BOUNDS THE POPULATION TO ONE, which is the inverse of the defect. Its own doc: 'Doubles as the reentry guard: an overlapping fire (double-fire, or a sweep outliving its window into the next grant) completes immediately instead of resetting the in-flight fire's state.' The sibling per-fire state that genuinely needs to be per-identity is already a Set (completedTaskIDs), with a comment explaining why a shared bool was wrong there.

A cooldown timestamp about the OBSERVER, not the identity of a member of any population — there is nothing it could name the wrong one of. One observer, one sweep cadence; the quantity is 'when did I last sweep' and a second concurrent reader would be asking the same question about the same subject.

Same shape as lastSweepAt: a scalar about the transport, feeding the post-seek skip-suppression window. Bounded to one by the product — there is exactly one playback session and one playhead. The per-episode identities this actor DOES key on (activeAssetId for windows and decisions) are already separate fields, so this is not standing in for any of them.

A single-artifact cache whose whole contract is last-writer-wins: there is one shared lexicon, versioned, and 'the newest verified artifact' is the value wanted. Backed by one on-disk file (shared-sponsor-lexicon-lkg.json), so the slot names the same singleton the filesystem does. Not an identity picked out of a set.
